tolerance.note: numbers relative 1e-6 (7 s.f.); residual compared abs 1e-9; errors compared exactly as {error: schema class, reason: lower_snake_case code} (KAT_SCHEMA 17:46)

convention: Steady state, no reaction unless stated, user-supplied consistent units. mix_temperature: adiabatic, constant cp per stream, no phase change; residual = sum m cp (T_i - T_out) must show 0. mix_concentration: complete mixing, conservative species. recycle: recycle_fraction r = share of the mixer outlet returned (0<=r<1). recycle_purge: fresh reactant A, single-pass conversion Xs, unreacted A fully separated and recycled less a purge fraction p of that stream; overall conversion = converted/fresh. recovery_cascade and manufacturing_yield: overall yield = product of step yields (0-1). atom_economy in % from user molar masses and stoichiometric coefficients. e_factor = waste/product mass. carbon_accounting: sum of qty x user-supplied factor (no factor database, scope cap); shares null when total is 0. mfa_balance: stock change = inputs - outputs. biomass_yield: X = Y_X/S x substrate consumed. At most 5 species, 10 streams, 1 recycle loop (scope cap).
oracle: script-verified (textbook formulae); ChatGPT Chat cross-check pending. Closed-form expected values from R. M. Felder & R. W. Rousseau, Elementary Principles of Chemical Processes (textbook); D. M. Himmelblau & J. B. Riggs, Basic Principles and Calculations in Chemical Engineering (textbook); M. L. Davis & D. A. Cornwell, Introduction to Environmental Engineering (textbook); B. M. Trost (1991), The atom economy, Science 254:1471; R. A. Sheldon (1992/2007), The E factor, Chem. Ind. / Green Chem. 9:1273; GHG Protocol Corporate Accounting and Reporting Standard (WRI/WBCSD), https://ghgprotocol.org/corporate-standard; P. H. Brunner & H. Rechberger, Handbook of Material Flow Analysis (textbook); R. G. Harrison et al., Bioseparations Science and Engineering (textbook); M. L. Shuler & F. Kargi, Bioprocess Engineering (textbook); recomputed independently by solving the stream balances as linear systems (numpy), successive substitution around the recycle loop, log-sum yields and math.fsum
